project.name: FlatBuffers
project.commit_note: Stage 01's authoritative crash evidence for this sample is the staged default MemorySanitizer trace saved in the result bundle. The staged ARVO workspace source is commit `71652195352f3b7cbafa7cb65af9f281204d51c4`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`, but it still contains the vulnerable `cursor_[4]` lookahead in `src/idl_parser.cpp` and the staged `patch.diff` changes that exact read to `cursor_[3]`; all line anchors below use the staged workspace line map.

staged_source_snapshot.description: Every source location below is anchored to this exact staged vulnerable snapshot inside the running ARVO workspace container.

classification.classification_note: The saved MSan report is triggered when `flatbuffers::Parser::Next()` branches on an off-by-one lookahead byte. Source-side, the defect is the signed-`inf` boundary check reading `cursor_[4]` instead of `cursor_[3]` after the logical end of the parser-visible string.

bug_description.original: An off-by-one error exists in the parser.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable workspace source
bug_description.normalized: The authoritative staged MemorySanitizer trace in `sanitizer_trace.txt` reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` in `flatbuffers::Parser::Next()` at `src/idl_parser.cpp:495:47` on the exact 64-byte staged `monster_fuzzer` witness. The first two witness bytes are the fuzzer header `31 94`: line 112 loads `0x31` into `flags`, line 123 computes `opts.strict_json = (flags & 0x80)`, and because that bit is clear the parser will accept bare JSON field names. Line 113 treats the second header byte as reserved, then lines 114-118 skip the 2-byte header, copy the remaining payload, and truncate it at the first NUL, so `input` becomes exact string `{test5:[[0,-inf` with its logical C-string terminator immediately after the `f`. Line 129 passes both that string and the header-derived options by value to `do_test`; line 74 stores `opts` in `parser_.opts`, line 77 calls `parser_.ParseJson(input_json.c_str())`, and `StartParseFile` stores the copied C string in parser state. While parsing the root object, `ParseTableDelimiters` reaches line 1216 with bare field token `test5`; because `opts.strict_json` is false, it accepts `kTokenIdentifier` instead of requiring a quoted string key, `ParseTable` resolves that key to `Monster.test5:[Test]`, `ParseAnyValue` dispatches into `ParseVector`, and the nested-array `ParseTable(Test)` path consumes `0,` before `ParseComma()` reaches `Parser::Next()` on the trailing signed `inf` for the second `Test` member. Vulnerable `Next()` correctly recognizes the sign and the following `"inf"`, but it checks the post-token boundary with `cursor_[4]` instead of `cursor_[3]`. Because `cursor_[3]` is already the copied string terminator, `cursor_[4]` branches on one byte beyond the initialized parser-visible payload in `input_json`, which is the saved MSan sink. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by changing both lookups from `cursor_[4]` to `cursor_[3]`. `reproduction_report.json` also records that the rebuilt ARVO workspace compile lacked MSan-instrumented libraries and its rerun only emitted raw `SIGSEGV`, so the saved staged trace is the authoritative crash evidence for this sample.

source.description: Parser-side materialization of the copied JSON C string. `StartParseFile` stores `do_test`'s `input_json.c_str()` in parser state and resets the parser cursor to walk that exact buffer after `do_test` has already loaded the header-derived parser options.
source.value_from: The staged witness begins with header bytes `31 94`. Byte 0 (`0x31`) clears `flags_strict_json`, so `do_test` has already stored `opts.strict_json = false` in `parser_.opts` before calling `ParseJson`. After the reserved second header byte is skipped, the payload begins `7b 74 65 73 74 35 3a 5b 5b 30 2c 2d 69 6e 66 00`, and the first NUL immediately after `f` makes the copied `input_json` string exact text `{test5:[[0,-inf` when this source step receives it.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: MemorySanitizer string origin. The harness truncates the post-header payload at the first NUL and stores the parser-visible text in stack-local `input`; line 129 then copies that string into callee-local `input_json`, whose C string is the one later read past its terminator. The separate first header byte controls parser mode but is not the string byte MSan tracks to the sink.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the staged `poc`, payload bytes after the 2-byte header are `{test5:[[0,-inf\0...`, so `input` becomes exactly `{test5:[[0,-inf` and the NUL after `f` is the last byte that belongs to that parser-visible string before `do_test` copies it into `input_json`.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer sink. The signed-`inf` boundary predicate branches on `cursor_[4]`, which on the reproducing input is one byte past the copied `input_json.c_str()` terminator after `-inf`.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/flatbuffers/src/idl_parser.cpp:495:47` in `flatbuffers::Parser::Next`, with callers `Expect` and `ParseComma`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The signed-`inf` tokenizer checks the byte after `inf` with `cursor_[4]` instead of `cursor_[3]`, so an input where `+/-inf` ends exactly at the copied string terminator reads one byte past the initialized parser-visible buffer in `input_json`.
root_cause.note: The staged `patch.diff` changes both lookups from `cursor_[4]` to `cursor_[3]`, confirming that the boundary test should stop at the actual character immediately following `inf`.

field_name_admitted.description: The root object starts with bare field name `test5`, not a quoted JSON string. Because header byte `0x31` leaves `opts.strict_json` clear, this expectation accepts `kTokenIdentifier`; if the strict-json flag were set, the witness would be rejected here before any `-inf` parsing.

parser_admitted.description: With the Monster schema already deserialized in `LLVMFuzzerInitialize`, and after line 1216 admits bare field `test5`, the truncated witness is processed as a root-object JSON parse. The saved crash stack later descends through `ParseTable -> ParseAnyValue -> ParseVector -> ParseComma -> Next` below this call.

evidence_limitations: The staged source snapshot is workspace commit `71652195352f3b7cbafa7cb65af9f281204d51c4`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `746c73b910f11fcf5da0b4727bce0909d8a573e4`; however the staged `patch.diff` fixes the same `Parser::Next()` lookahead there, and the saved sanitizer trace resolves against that staged line map.

The rebuilt ARVO workspace compile warned that it was built without MSan-instrumented libraries, and the rerun only produced raw `SIGSEGV` in `/out/monster_fuzzer`; crash-site facts therefore rely on the staged default MemorySanitizer trace that `reproduction_report.json` marks as authoritative.

MemorySanitizer origin tracking names the stack allocation of fuzzer-local `input`, and its store-to-memory stack points to the line-129 copy into `input_json`, but it does not identify the exact internal byte offset read past the terminator. That final byte position and reachability are established source-side from the staged `poc`'s first header byte clearing `opts.strict_json`, the unquoted `test5` admission at line 1216, the first NUL after `-inf`, the `input -> input_json -> ParseJson -> StartParseFile` propagation chain, and the vulnerable `cursor_[4]` read.

fine_trace.note: The first witness byte `0x31` is a load-bearing control input, not a discarded prefix byte. The harness reads it as parser flags, and its `flags_strict_json` bit (`0x80`) is clear.

After consuming the 2-byte fuzzer header, the harness copies the remaining 62 bytes and truncates them at the first NUL. For the staged `poc`, the reserved second header byte is skipped and `input` becomes exact string `{test5:[[0,-inf`, so its C-string terminator sits immediately after `f` even though more raw witness bytes remain in `original`.

The header byte from step 1 is translated into parser mode: `0x31 & 0x80 == 0`, so `opts.strict_json` becomes false. The bare field name `test5` in the staged payload will therefore be admissible later.

fine_trace.code: const std::string jsongen_1 = do_test(opts, input, false);
fine_trace.note: This call passes both the header-derived options and the truncated string by value. The `do_test` parameter `input_json` is copy-constructed from exact text `{test5:[[0,-inf`, and the saved MSan store-to-memory stack points to this call site because the `std::string` copy constructor propagates the shadow state from `input` into callee-local `input_json`.
The header-derived parser mode is written into parser state. From here on, `opts.strict_json` remains false inside `parser_`, which directly controls root field-name admission at line 1216.
After step 5 primes parser mode, this call passes the copied `input_json` C string into the parser. From here onward the parser walks the callee-local copy, not the caller's `input` object.

Source. `source` is the `input_json.c_str()` pointer from step 6. `StartParseFile` stores that attacker-controlled C string and resets parser state so `cursor_` walks the truncated `{test5:[[0,-inf` buffer.

When parsing the root object after the opening `{`, the bare field name starts with identifier byte `t`. This branch collects `test5` and classifies it as `kTokenIdentifier` rather than as a quoted string token.

With current field token from step 8, this predicate uses parser mode from step 5 to decide what kind of key is legal. Because `opts.strict_json` is false, the bare `test5` key is accepted as `kTokenIdentifier` and parsing continues into value `[[0,-inf`.

Inside the root `Monster` table parse, admitted key `test5` resolves to the known schema field `test5:[Test]`. That lookup fixes the downstream value type as a vector whose elements are `Test` structs.

For `Monster.test5`, `field->value.type.base_type` is `BASE_TYPE_VECTOR` and its element type is `Test`. `ParseAnyValue` therefore dispatches the field value into `ParseVector` instead of scalar parsing.

This vector parser enters `ParseVectorDelimiters` for the outer `[` of `[[0,-inf`. On the first element (`count == 0`), it sets the element value type to `Test` and dispatches parsing with current token already on the inner `[` that starts that struct initializer.
Because the current vector element type from step 12 is struct `Test`, `ParseAnyValue` recurses into `ParseTable(Test)` on the inner `[` instead of treating the element as a scalar.

With `struct_def == Test` and current token `[` from step 13, the parser enters nested-array struct mode. `NEXT()` consumes that inner bracket, then unnamed field index 0 resolves to `Test.a`, so the following literal `0` is parsed as the first struct member.

For `Test.a` (a scalar short), `ParseAnyValue` uses `ParseSingleValue` to consume the literal `0`. When that scalar parse returns, the current token has advanced to the separating comma after the first unnamed struct member.

After step 15, the nested `Test` initializer is not finished and the current token is `,`, so `ParseComma` expects that separator. Its nested `Expect(',')` call will invoke `Next()` to fetch the next unnamed field value, which begins with `-` for `Test.b`.
Reached from step 16's `Expect(',')`, `Next()` reads the next token's leading `'-'` byte from the copied `input_json` buffer and advances `cursor_` to the following `i` in `inf`.
The current token starts with a sign, so `Next()` enters the signed-number special case instead of falling through to identifier handling.
At the advanced cursor position, the next three bytes are exactly `i`, `n`, `f`, so the signed-`inf` fast path is taken and the code proceeds to the post-token boundary check.

Root cause and sink. For the copied `input_json` buffer, `cursor_[0..2]` are `i`, `n`, `f` and `cursor_[3]` is the string terminator immediately after `f`, but this predicate reads `cursor_[4]` instead of `cursor_[3]`. That one-byte lookahead branches on a byte beyond the initialized parser-visible payload in callee-local `input_json`, and the branch itself is the saved MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value. The staged patch changes both lookups to `cursor_[3]`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Allocation context points to the fuzzer-local `input` object; the saved store-to-memory stack then shows line 129 copying that state into callee-local `input_json`, and `Parser::Next()` later reads past the terminator of that copied parser-visible string.

poc.trigger: The exact staged 64-byte witness uses header byte `0x31` to keep `opts.strict_json` clear and uses the post-header payload to build exact parser string `{test5:[[0,-inf`; the parser therefore accepts the unquoted root field `test5`, later reaches the signed-`inf` tokenizer in `Parser::Next`, and the authoritative staged MemorySanitizer trace reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` when that tokenizer branches on `cursor_[4]`.

format.name: monster_fuzzer input: 1-byte parser flags, 1 reserved byte, then NUL-truncated JSON text
format.contract: Use the exact 64-byte staged witness. Byte 0 must be `0x31` so `flags & flags_strict_json` leaves `opts.strict_json` false; byte 1 is the reserved header byte and is skipped. Starting at byte 2, the payload must begin `7b 74 65 73 74 35 3a 5b 5b 30 2c 2d 69 6e 66 00` so the harness constructs `input` as exact string `{test5:[[0,-inf`. The trigger relies on that bare `test5` field being admitted at line 1216 as `kTokenIdentifier`, then on `Parser::Next()` reaching the signed-`inf` fast path with `cursor_[0..2] == 'i','n','f'`, `cursor_[3] == '\0'`, and the vulnerable code still reading `cursor_[4]`. This GT is grounded only for that exact staged witness and observed flag/truncation behavior, not all malformed FlatBuffers JSON inputs or all `+/-inf` spellings.
